title: OpenAI API key
description: OpenAI API key with Realtime access: the voice, unless `VOICE_BASE_URL` names a server of your own, and the voice model's `web_search`.

title: Realtime model
description: The realtime speech-to-speech model a call runs on, on OpenAI. A voice server elsewhere is sent it too (as `?model=`); the voice pipeline here never is.

title: Assistant name
description: What the assistant on the phone is called: the name it answers to and introduces itself by. Lyra and Jarvis each bring a voice of their own; any other name — letters, spaces, apostrophes and hyphens, up to 32 — speaks in `OPENAI_VOICE`, or `marin`.

title: Assistant voice
description: The Realtime voice the assistant speaks in. Empty is the assistant's own (`ASSISTANT_NAME`); a voice the key's organization may not use makes every call fail to open. Sent to OpenAI only, and for one release to a voice server elsewhere that has no `VOICE_SERVER_VOICE`.

title: Transcription model
description: Transcribes what the caller says, for the call log, on OpenAI; a voice of your own transcribes with its own speech-to-text.

title: Transcription language
description: The language you speak on a call, as an ISO-639-1 code (`en`, `de`, `fr`), for the call log's transcription — which `recall` and the memory read. Empty lets the transcriber guess each turn. The voice model itself hears the audio either way.

title: Clock format
description: How the voice prompt writes the time of day (`14:05` or `2:05 PM`), and so how the assistant tends to say it.

title: Voice pipeline
description: How a call's voice is built: `speech-to-speech`, one model that hears and speaks (OpenAI, or a Realtime server elsewhere), or `three-model`, speech-to-text, an LLM and text-to-speech (the voice here). Blank is the only one `VOICE_MODE` offers today; one it does not offer is refused.

title: Web search model
description: Answers the voice model's own `web_search` tool, through the Responses API (the Realtime API has no hosted search tool).

title: Turn detection
description: How the assistant decides you have finished: `semantic` waits on whether the sentence sounds finished, so a pause to think does not cut you off; `server` is a plain silence timer of `VAD_SILENCE_MS`.

title: Reply eagerness
description: Semantic mode only: `low` waits longest, `high` jumps in soonest, `auto` is `medium`.

title: Silence to end a turn (ms)
description: Server mode only: the silence, in milliseconds, that ends a turn.

title: Speech threshold
description: Server mode only: how loud counts as speech (0 to 1).

title: Audio before speech (ms)
description: Server mode only: audio kept from before speech was detected, so the first syllable is not clipped.

title: Noise reduction
description: Background-noise suppression on what the model hears; `auto` picks `near_field` for a phone and `far_field` for a microphone across the room. Mostly about barge-in: noise mistaken for speech is noise that cuts the assistant off.

title: Default agent
description: The coding agent a task runs on when nobody names one out loud. The running service may switch it only among `AGENTS_ENABLED`.

title: Enabled agents
description: Every agent a task may be sent to, comma-separated; blank is `AGENT_BACKEND` alone. `keryx serve` refuses a default that is not in here.

title: Time limit per task (seconds)
description: The longest one subagent run may take, on any agent, in seconds; 0 is no limit.

title: Anthropic API key
description: Claude, paid per token. Set, it wins over the subscription.

title: Claude subscription token
description: Claude on your subscription, for a machine with no browser: the token `claude setup-token` prints. Blank uses the stored `claude` login.

title: Claude model
description: The model a Claude task runs on when none is named.

title: Turns per task
description: Agent turns one Claude task may take.

title: Budget per task (USD)
description: Dollars one Claude task may spend: a runaway cap. On a subscription it is the SDK's estimate of what the task would have cost, not a charge.

title: Codex API key
description: Codex, paid per token. Keryx logs in with it once, into its own `CODEX_HOME`; `OPENAI_API_KEY` is never used for Codex.

title: Codex subscription token
description: Codex on your ChatGPT plan, for a machine with no browser. Blank uses the stored `codex login`.

title: Codex model
description: The model a Codex task runs on; blank is Codex's own default.

title: Where the voice runs
description: Where a call's voice runs: `openai` is OpenAI Realtime, `here` the speech pipeline on this machine (`VOICE_SERVER_*`), `server` a Realtime server elsewhere (`VOICE_BASE_URL`). Blank is worked out from `VOICE_BASE_URL`, as it was before this was a setting: blank is OpenAI, this machine's voice port is here, any other address a server.

title: Voice server URL
description: A voice server of your own that speaks the OpenAI Realtime protocol, as its `…/v1` address (`http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1` is the one `keryx setup` installs). Blank is OpenAI.

title: Voice server API key
description: The Bearer key for that voice server, when it checks one.

title: Speech-to-text model
description: How the local voice server hears: speech-to-speech's `--stt` (`parakeet-tdt`, `whisper`, …).

title: Voice LLM
description: Where the words of a voice running here come from: `shared` is the local agent's model on its server, `here` a model of the voice's own (`VOICE_LLM_MODEL`) on a server of its own on this machine, `remote` a server elsewhere (`VOICE_LLM_BASE_URL`) — a box of yours, or a cloud's Responses API.

title: Voice LLM model
description: The voice LLM's model. With `VOICE_LLM=here`, a name from `keryx models list` or a GGUF file's path, served under that name; with `remote`, the server's own name for it. Not read while the voice LLM is shared.

title: Voice LLM server URL
description: With `VOICE_LLM=remote`, the server the voice's words go to, as its `…/v1` address (`https://api.openai.com/v1` for OpenAI's).

title: Voice LLM API key
description: The Bearer key for that server, when it checks one. Blank sends `OPENAI_API_KEY` only when the address is OpenAI's own, and no key of yours anywhere else.

title: Text-to-speech model
description: How the local voice server speaks: speech-to-speech's `--tts` (`kokoro`, `qwen3`, …).

title: Kokoro voice
description: The Kokoro voice the local voice server speaks in (`af_heart`, `bm_george`, …; `keryx models list` shows them). A voice server elsewhere is sent it too, once it is set.

title: Extra voice server flags
description: More flags for `speech-to-speech serve`, as a command line — a smaller speech model (`--stt_model_name openai/whisper-base`), a TTS speed. Never a key: it is on argv.

title: Local agent server URL
description: An inference server for the `local` agent — Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio — as `http://gpu-box:11434` or its `…/v1` address. Blank is no local agent.

title: Local agent API key
description: The Bearer key for that server, when it checks one. The owner's Anthropic and OpenAI credentials are never sent there.

title: Local agent model
description: The model a `local` task runs on, by the server's own name for it.

title: Local agent harness
description: Which harness drives the local model: `anthropic-messages` runs it inside Claude Code, `openai-responses` inside Codex. The server must speak that API.

title: Agent model to serve
description: The model the local agent's llama.cpp server on this machine runs: a name from `keryx models list`, or a GGUF file's path. Blank runs none.

title: Agent model server port
description: The port the local agent's llama.cpp server binds, on 127.0.0.1.

title: Voice server port
description: The port the local voice server binds, on 127.0.0.1.

title: Voice LLM server port
description: The port the voice LLM's own llama.cpp server binds, on 127.0.0.1, with `VOICE_LLM=here`.

title: Your name
description: What the assistant calls you in the prompts it is handed; blank is "the owner". Only a name: the rest of what it knows about you is its memory.

title: Your phone numbers
description: Your phone numbers in E.164 (`+15551234567`), comma-separated. Every other caller is refused. This is the handsets one person picks up, not a guest list: a call Keryx places to any of them reached you.

title: Number to ring first
description: Which of your numbers Keryx rings first; blank is the first of `ALLOWED_CALLERS`.

title: Phone PIN
description: The phone PIN: 6 to 8 digits, asked for before anything is dispatched from a call. Not kept in the configuration files: it lives in `KERYX_HOME/pin`, written once by `keryx setup` or by the first call, and this variable, set in the environment, overrides that file. With no PIN anywhere nothing of yours is read out on the phone and every dispatch is refused.

title: Wrong PINs before lockout
description: Wrong PINs, counted across every call, before PIN entry locks for everyone — the right PIN included.

title: Wrong PINs remembered (hours)
description: How long a wrong PIN is remembered.

title: Lockout length (minutes)
description: How long PIN entry stays locked once the limit is reached.

title: Briefing before the PIN
description: Whether a call is handed its standing briefing — unreported results, the memory, project names, briefs, skills — before the PIN. The PIN is the line between reading and acting; off means nothing of yours is said until it is given. Does nothing until a PIN exists.

title: Twilio account SID
description: Your Twilio account SID (`AC…`).

title: Twilio auth token
description: Your Twilio auth token.

title: Twilio number
description: The Twilio number Keryx answers and calls from, in E.164.

title: Text messages (SMS)
description: Whether Keryx may text at all. Off: many Twilio accounts cannot send SMS in their region, and Slack is the written channel. Outbound calls are unaffected.

title: Public hostname
description: The public hostname Twilio reaches this machine on, e.g. `keryx.example.com`: the name routed to your tunnel.

title: Cloudflare tunnel
description: The Cloudflare tunnel the service scripts run (`scripts/dev.sh`, `scripts/install-systemd.sh`).

title: Phone server address
description: The address the phone server binds.

title: Phone server port
description: The port the phone server binds.

title: OAuth client ID
description: The Google OAuth client id. Blank: read from `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRETS_FILE`.

title: OAuth client secret
description: The Google OAuth client secret, with the id above.

title: OAuth client file
description: The OAuth client JSON the Google Cloud console downloads (desktop or web shape). Blank: `KERYX_HOME/google_client_secret.json`, where `keryx setup` puts it.

title: Google account
description: The Google account agents act as; `keryx setup` fills it in from the sign-in.

title: Workspace MCP server
description: Give every subagent the workspace-mcp server (send mail, manage the calendar). Needed for Codex, which has no claude.ai connectors; Claude already has them.

title: Slack bot token
description: The bot token the `send_to_slack` plugin posts with (and the PIN-lockout alert).

title: OpenAI admin key
description: An OpenAI *admin* key for the `check_billing` plugin; the ordinary key gets a 401 on the costs endpoint.

title: Anthropic admin key
description: An `sk-ant-admin…` key, for what the subagents have cost (`check_billing`).

title: Other projects
description: Spoken project names for repositories outside `PROJECTS_ROOT`, as `{"name": "/path"}`.

title: Projects folder
description: Where a task with no project starts; each subdirectory is a project you can name. Never created: without it, such a task starts in `DATA_DIR/workspace`.

title: Skills folder
description: Where the Claude CLI keeps its skills; listed in the voice prompt so the assistant knows what the subagents are good at.

title: Keryx checkout
description: The Keryx repository on this machine, which a subagent reads when it reports a problem with Keryx. Unset: the checkout Keryx runs from, when it runs from one.

title: GitHub issue reports
description: Whether a bug or a feature request for Keryx, said on a call, may be filed as a GitHub issue by a subagent, with `gh`. `keryx setup` asks; only you can turn it on.

title: Issue repository
description: The GitHub repository (`owner/name`) those issues are filed on.

title: Approval calls
description: Whether a Claude Code prompt left unanswered on your screen may become a call. The hook is installed separately (`scripts/install-claude-hook.sh`).

title: Ring after (seconds)
description: How long a prompt waits on screen before Keryx rings about it.

title: Answer window (seconds)
description: How long the hook keeps waiting after that. The two together are the longest the hook blocks; its `timeout` in `~/.claude/settings.json` must exceed their sum.

title: Maximum calls per hour
description: Approval calls per hour, however many prompts pile up.

title: Quiet hours
description: `HH:MM-HH:MM` in which it never rings (may cross midnight), in the host's time.

title: Allowed commands
description: The only shell commands a keypad digit may ever run, matched word for word; only `git push` and `git commit` may carry arguments (`keryx/approvals/policy.py`). This allowlist is the primary control: widening it widens exactly what a phone keypad can execute.

title: Writable folders
description: Where a file may be written by phone approval; blank is `PROJECTS_ROOT` plus every project in `PROJECTS`.

title: Tasks at once
description: Subagents running at once; the rest queue.

title: Inline answer wait (seconds)
description: How long a call waits for a short task to answer inline.

title: Local session timeout (seconds)
description: Seconds of silence that end a local session; 0 never does.

title: Maximum call length (seconds)
description: The longest a phone call may run; Keryx wraps up 30 s before. 0 is no limit.

title: Phone calls at once
description: Phone calls open at once, each one a realtime session being paid for; another hears that the line is busy.

title: Tasks per day
description: Tasks dispatched per day.

title: Keep transcripts for (days)
description: Delete call transcripts older than this many days; 0 keeps everything.

title: Keep finished tasks for (days)
description: Delete finished tasks older than this; 0 keeps everything. A result you have not been told about is never deleted.

title: Data folder
description: Where tasks, transcripts, memory and sign-in tokens are kept, owner-only (0700, files 0600).

title: State folder
description: Where the logs, the restart record and the approval bridge's socket are kept, owner-only.

title: Cache folder
description: Where what can be downloaded again is kept.

title: Service manager
description: What `keryx restart` asks to restart this process: `auto` is systemd or launchd, but only for a process actually running under it; `none` refuses.

title: Service unit or label
description: The systemd unit or launchd label; blank is the installed default (`keryx.service`, `dev.keryx.agent`).

title: Report link secret
description: Signs the `/reports/{id}` links texted to you; blank generates one into `DATA_DIR/report_secret`.

title: Log level
description: How much `STATE_DIR/logs/keryx.log` says.

title: Skip Twilio signatures
description: Skip Twilio's request signatures, for a machine nothing outside can reach. `keryx serve` refuses the phone with it on behind a `PUBLIC_HOST`.

title: Demo mode
description: Try the phone before a coding agent is set up: calls, the PIN and call-backs are real, and every task comes back after a moment with a sample answer that says it was a demo. No agent runs and no agent tokens are spent. `keryx serve --demo` turns it on for one run.
